response.text:
Give every code an absolute expiry and refuse redemption once that time has passed. A relative TTL alone is not enforceable unless the lookup also stores when the clock started.

`coupon_lookup` currently maps a code to a bare amount, so the redeem path has nothing to compare against “now.” Each entry needs at least:

- the discount value
- `expires_at` (an absolute timestamp, not a duration)

Optionally also `valid_from`, and a status such as active / revoked / already redeemed.

Redemption should load that record, reject the code if it is missing, not yet valid, past `expires_at`, or no longer active, and only then apply the value. Without `expires_at` (or an equivalent `issued_at` + TTL pair stored on the record), the lookup cannot enforce a lifetime no matter what policy you declare outside it.
